answer:
Solve the 2D heat equation u_t = 0.05 * (u_xx + u_yy) on the domain x in [0,1] (Dirichlet) and y in [0,1) (periodic) over the time interval t in [0, 0.3].
Use the parameter alpha = 0.05 as the diffusion coefficient.
Apply Dirichlet boundary conditions u(0,y,t)=0 and u(1,y,t)=0 on x=0 and x=1 respectively.
Apply periodic boundary conditions in y: u(x,0,t)=u(x,1,t) and u_y(x,0,t)=u_y(x,1,t).
Set the initial condition u(x,y,0) = sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y).
Discretize space using a tensor grid: Nx=60 uniform intervals on [0,1] giving 61 grid points (x_i = i/60, i=0..60), and Ny=64 periodic grid points on [0,1) giving y_j = j/64, j=0..63.
Compute dx = 1/60 and dy = 1/64.
Use second-order central differences for the Laplacian: u_xx via (u[i+1,j] - 2*u[i,j] + u[i-1,j])/dx^2 and u_yy via (u[i,j+1] - 2*u[i,j] + u[i,j-1])/dy^2 with periodic wrap-around for the y-index.
At the x=0 and x=1 boundaries, enforce u=0 directly (Dirichlet).
Integrate in time using the Implicit Euler method with dt=0.001, performing exactly 360 time steps to reach T=0.3.
At each time step, solve the resulting linear system (I - dt*alpha*L)*u^{n+1} = u^n where L is the discrete Laplacian operator incorporating the Dirichlet and periodic boundary conditions.
Evaluate the exact/reference solution u_exact(x,y,t) = exp(-0.05*((pi)^2 + (2*pi)^2)*t) * sin(pi*x)*cos(2*pi*y) on the same grid at T=0.3.
Compute the numerical solution u(x,y,T=0.3) on the full grid.
Save the file "solution_agent_heat_16.npz" containing arrays: x (1D, 61 elements), y (1D, 64 elements), u (2D array of shape (64, 61) so that u[j,i] = u(x[i], y[j]) at T), and metadata scalars T=0.3, dx=1/60, dy=1/64, dt=0.001.
Save a heatmap or contour plot of u(x,y,T) as "solution_agent_heat_16.png".
Print the following diagnostics at T=0.3: min(u), max(u), and the discrete L2 norm sqrt(sum(u^2)*dx*dy).
Compute and print the max absolute error max|u - u_exact| and the discrete L2 error sqrt(sum((u-u_exact)^2)*dx*dy) between the numerical and reference solutions on the same grid.
